items.body: [PLAYLIST] Kurator Mike Patricola und das Label Smiling C – das Team hinter Voice of Love – sind zurück. Pipe Dreams heißt die neue Compilation, die am 23. Oktober erscheinen wird. Sie enthält 19 vergessene Songs, aufgenommen zwischen Ende der 1970er und Mitte der 1980er, die – nun ja – nah am Wasser gebaut sind. Wortwörtlich. Seite A klassischer Yacht Rock, Seite B Surf-Disco, Seite C zeigt intimere »tropische Troubadoure«, Seite D schließt die Klammer mit Yacht-Rock. Not Only Surfin‘ U.S.A Die versammelten Interpret:innen kommen nicht nur aus den USA, sondern auch aus Australien, Japan, Kanada, Frankreich, von den Bahamas oder von Hawaii. Die Compilation zeigt Yacht Rock nicht als eine auf Kalifornien begrenzte, sondern als globale Ästhetik. Der Japaner Twin Cosmos legt auf »Coconuts Wind« eine Lennon erinnernde Melodie in eine lauwarme Meeresbrise. Pierre Rochette aus Montréal träumt sich mit afrikanischen Rhythmen und Disco-Gitarren-Grooves »On The Beach«. Miles Corbin Rick Sharp Twin Cosmos Die auf schwarzem Vinyl gepresste Schallplatte erscheint in einem luxuriösen, gestanzten Gatefold-Cover mit Spotlackierung und ist auf dem europäischen Festland exklusiv bei HHV erhältlich. Das Artwork stammt von Charles Bals und basiert auf dem Foto »Breaking Wave« von Lex Thompson. Im HHV Shop kaufenV.A.Pipe Dreams HHV EU Exclusive Black Vinyl Editionab 47.99€
items._genre: yacht rock / soft rock / disco / global pop
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由Smiling C厂牌发行，收录了19首1970年代末至1980年代中期被遗忘的曲目，以'水'为主题将它们串联起来。唱片分为四面：经典Yacht Rock、Surf-Disco、热带游吟诗人以及回归Yacht Rock。选曲覆盖美国、澳大利亚、日本、加拿大、法国、巴哈马和夏威夷等地，试图打破Yacht Rock仅限于加州的地域刻板印象，展示其作为一种全球美学的面貌。日本艺人Twin Cosmos在《Coconuts Wind》中呈现类Lennon式旋律与海洋氛围的结合，加拿大蒙特利尔的Pierre Rochette则在《On The Beach》中融入非洲节奏与迪斯科吉他律动。唱片采用黑胶压制，配以手工穿孔的Gatefold封面，附Spot UV工艺，由HHV在欧洲独家发行。作为一篇产品推介类新闻稿，内容偏向商业信息介绍，缺乏深入的乐评分析。

items._cn_summary: 本文为1966年《Jazz Journal》杂志对Le Roi Jones（后改名Amiri Baraka）所著《Blues People》一书的回顾评论。该书探讨非裔美国人在爵士乐发展中的核心地位，批判白人乐评对爵士的挪用，并触及中产阶级黑人社区与种族融合等议题。文章本身是爵士乐文化评论类文字，并非音乐录音作品，内容聚焦于种族政治与音乐文化批判的关系。作为历史性书评，其与当代音乐实践关联有限，且原文摘录过短，难以判断论述深度与原创性。对关注学院派爵士与自由即兴的听众而言，此书是理解1960年代黑人艺术运动与先锋爵士思想史的重要文献，但作为乐评本身信息量不足，难以充分评估其文本质量与学术价值。

items.body: French print fanzine Lumières Noires has released its third issue, “Lumières Noires Fanzine N°3”, out now on Bandcamp. The zine is founded and edited by Vincent Dromard and covers underground and dark music. Printed in a run of 104 hand-numbered copies, the issue comes in A5 format with a glossy hardcover, 124 pages in color and black-and-white, perfect-bound and digitally printed. The text is in French. Lumières Noires Fanzine N°3 covers Pharmakon (harsh noise, visceral industrial – USA), Rosemary Loves A Blackberry / Diana Burkot (electronic art pop – Iceland/Russia), Jennifer Touch (dark acidwave – Germany), Ailise Blake (cosmic neofolk – Italy/France), Dermabrasion (death rock, disco punk – Canada), Madeline Goldstein (wet new wave – USA), Hilary Woods (blinding black drone folk – Ireland) and Robin Kester (psychedelic pop, electro rock – Netherlands), plus Buzzkill (coldwave, steel-hard punk – France), along with more than fifty reviews of vinyl, CD, cassette and VHS releases. Dromard, who runs the fanzine from France, described the issue as dedicated “to underground music.” About Lumières Noires Fanzine Lumières Noires is a French print fanzine covering underground and dark music, founded and edited by Vincent Dromard. Its first issue was released in March 2025 after six months of work, printed in 108 hand-numbered copies: A5 format, glossy hardcover, 112 pages in color and black-and-white, perfect-bound and digitally printed. That issue included interviews and features on artists such as Kælan Mikla and Denuit, alongside about fifty reviews of physical releases. The second issue followed around November 2025, printed in 100 hand-numbered copies in the same A5 glossy hardcover format, 116 pages in color and black-and-white, perfect-bound and digitally printed. It featured Ic3peak, Left For Pleasure, Donna Blue, Systeme Paradoxe, Blanche Biau, Dlina Volny, Babel Map, La Punta Bianca and Violent Vickie, plus fifty-four reviews of vinyl, CD, cassette and DVD releases; each order included a 40×30 cm poster. Lumières Noires Fanzine N°3, released in September 2026, is the third issue since the zine launched, and is available on Bandcamp alongside the first two.
items._cn_summary: 本文并非乐评，而是法国印刷刊物《Lumières Noires Fanzine》第三期的发行资讯。主编 Vincent Dromard 以手工编号限量104本的A5精装形式呈现地下与暗潮音乐场景，涵盖 Pharmakon 的严酷噪音与内脏工业、Dermabrasion 的死亡摇滚与迪斯科朋克、Hilary Woods 的黑色 drone folk 等横跨多国的暗潮与实验音乐人作品，并附有超过五十张黑胶、CD、卡带与VHS唱片的评论。前两期分别于2025年3月与11月发行，访谈对象包括 Kælan Mikla、Ic3peak、Dlina Volny 等。本文未对任何特定专辑进行深入的音乐分析或审美评判，仅为刊物的内容简介与出版信息说明。

items.body: Review by Grumpyprogfan — Quivira is the name of a road close to where I live. And with three reviewers hailing this a "masterpiece" and referencing the band Kansas - well, I had to check this out. I consider "Leftoverture" a masterpiece, this... no. The musicans are: Lisa LaRue, composer, keys, drum and computer programming; John Baker, guitar, bass, vocals; Jake Livgreen, vocals; With... Joe Deninzon, violin, and Evan Stanley, guitar, each play on one song. So this is really a duo. The musicians are quite good and Lisa's compositions are good, but it has a Neal Morse / Flying Colors vibe more than a Kansas vibe, for me. I like that Quivira has lots of instrumental sections - where the musicians can jam - because the vocals are far from the majestic duo that was Steinhardt and Walsh. In fact, there aren't many vocals on this album at all. Overall, this is a good debut album, and if you enjoy a mostly instrumental retro 70's style of music, Quivira could be worth a listen. I'm curious is this a one-off, or is a second album with a human drummer a possibility? Solid 3.25 stars.

items.body: Shostakovich was thirty when he wrote his Symphony No. 5 in 1937, the year after the Communist Party newspaper Pravda attacked his opera Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District. His Fourth Symphony had been withdrawn during rehearsals, announced as his own decision, though the pressure behind it is well documented. The Fifth’s Leningrad premiere under Yevgeny Mravinsky drew a long ovation and restored his position with the authorities. In the press the symphony was soon called a Soviet artist’s creative reply to just criticism, a line the composer never wrote but never disowned. The scoring is for a large orchestra with piano, celesta, harps and a full percussion section. Four movements run from a broad Moderato to a fast finale, by way of a short scherzo and a Largo that leaves the brass silent. The strings begin the work alone with a wide-leaping figure, and the finale turns its D minor into a loud D major. Whether that ending is genuine triumph or forced rejoicing has been argued for decades, and the second reading rests largely on Testimony, a memoir of disputed authenticity. Conductors answer the question in performance, above all in how fast they take the coda. Here are The Classic Review editorial team’s recommendations for the 10 best recordings of Shostakovich’s Symphony No. 5. Leningrad Philharmonic Orchestra, Yevgeny Mravinsky Mravinsky gave the first performance of the Fifth in 1937, and this concert recording, made forty-six years later, is his last word on it. Age had taken nothing from his hold on the score. The playing is fierce, and the shape of each movement stays clear under pressure. The finale sets off at a speed that sounds dangerous, then broadens at the close into something implacable. He pays no attention to the tempo mark printed at that point, and the ending is stronger for it. The orchestra is not always immaculate and a cough or two carries from the hall, but nothing else here has quite this authority. Mravinsky Amazon Presto New York Philharmonic, Leonard Bernstein Played as a virtuoso showpiece, the symphony gains a thrill it loses in graver hands. Bernstein had conducted it in the Soviet Union weeks earlier, with the composer in the hall and delighted by what he heard. This recording followed at home that October. The finale is the fastest here by a distance, and it takes the closing pages as plain triumph, with no hint that the rejoicing is forced. That choice divides listeners, and some find four movements at this pitch exhausting. For anyone who wants the ending to sound like a victory, this is the one. Bernstein Amazon Presto Apple London Symphony Orchestra, André Previn Refinement and drive rarely sit together in this symphony, but Previn found both in 1965 with the London Symphony Orchestra. The playing is rich and full, and nothing sounds rushed even where the tempos are quick. He puts his weight on the slow movement, which he lets stretch out and takes down to a whisper. The scherzo is the other high point, with the cellos and basses biting into the dance. His finale runs close to the speed printed in the score, nearer Bernstein than the slower modern versions. The transfer has its costs. Climaxes are a little flattened and rumble is audible in parts of the first movement, yet this is still one of the finest accounts of its era. Previn Amazon Presto Apple Berlin Symphony Orchestra, Kurt Sanderling Hearing this 1982 recording after the others is like having the score opened out on the table. Sanderling was in the hall for a Moscow performance weeks after the premiere, and in 1949 he conducted the concert that brought the work back into Soviet programs. What he offers is not weight or theater but clarity. The first movement is measured, the loud passages are scaled so that nothing is buried, and inner parts that usually pass unnoticed come through. High strings can sound a little glassy at the top, a small price for a reading that feels closer than any other here to the man who wrote the symphony. Sanderling Amazon Presto Apple Royal Concertgebouw Orchestra, Bernard Haitink Steadiness rather than terror is what Haitink offers in this 1981 recording. The orchestra is superb, the recorded sound warm and open, and the opening movement lands with real impact. What Haitink withholds is menace. The manner stays level where others press harder, the woodwind entries in the slow movement could be sharper, and the coda is finely judged where others are defiant. Some listeners want more horror from this symphony than they will find here. As orchestral playing, though, it is hard to beat. Haitink Amazon Presto Apple Royal Liverpool Philharmonic Orchestra, Vasily Petrenko Everything in Petrenko’s 2008 account is shaped by what happens at the end, and what happens at the end is a refusal to celebrate. He travels between extremes of loud and soft that few others attempt, and the detail he uncovers on the way is remarkable. The last movement holds a central stretch full of regret before the coda arrives at a crawl, closer to defiance than to victory. It is a hard listen by design, and not everyone will want the symphony to end this way. A few of his tempo shifts sound deliberate where they should feel inevitable, but nothing here states the case for the hollow ending more powerfully. Petrenko Amazon Presto Apple Pittsburgh Symphony Orchestra, Manfred Honeck Take the dynamic and balance markings literally, as Honeck does in this 2013 concert recording, and the symphony changes character. Details that normally sink into the texture come through clearly: the harp in the first movement, the piano at the climax of the Largo. Neither is a discovery, since both are in the score, but they are seldom this audible. The slow movement is the peak here, carried with dignity and a kind of quiet grief, never pressed for effect. He takes his time throughout, and the scherzo loses some of its irony as a result. Few recordings, though, let you hear so much of what is actually on the page. Honeck Amazon Presto Apple Boston Symphony Orchestra, Andris Nelsons The Boston Symphony Orchestra plays magnificently here, with trumpets that would be hard to better in any recent recording of this music. Nelsons keeps a current of unease running from the opening bars, and it never quite lets up, even in the passages that offer relief. One of those comes midway through the first movement, where the flute and horn answer each other over the strings and the music opens out for a moment. The sound is spacious, though there is a shade too much reverberation at the start for the string playing to register cleanly. No modern version sounds bigger, a broad canvas where Petrenko is lean. Nelsons Amazon Presto Apple London Symphony Orchestra, Maxim Shostakovich Maxim Shostakovich takes the symphony more slowly than anyone else here, well over ten minutes longer than Mravinsky across the four movements. The pulse never sags, which is what makes the approach work. The London Symphony Orchestra plays with complete seriousness. His slow movement refuses to plead. Feeling is held back instead of displayed, and the restraint is what makes it land. The finale’s march moves at a pace that cannot be hurried, with a central episode where real warmth breaks through, and its scale becomes the argument. Maxim Shostakovich Amazon Presto Apple Moscow Philharmonic Orchestra, Kirill Kondrashin By 1964 the symphony was nearly thirty years old, but this recording catches it as though the ink were still wet. Kondrashin, who gave the premieres of two of the composer’s symphonies and recorded the first complete cycle, drives the outer movements harder and rougher than almost any rival. Polish is not the point. Urgency is, and the coda in particular lands with a force smoother versions never find. The engineering shows its age, and this is not always the first Fifth recommended from his cycle. For anyone who wants the symphony at its most dangerous, it is still the obvious choice. items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于肖斯塔科维奇《第五交响曲》十大录音版本的推荐乐评。文章首先梳理了作品的创作背景——1937年首演，正值《真理报》批判其歌剧《姆岑斯克县的麦克白夫人》之后，作品最终被官方解读为对批评的创造性回应。评论随后逐一品评三款经典录音：穆拉文斯基1983年列宁格勒爱乐的实况录音以其权威性与终曲速度处理见长；伯恩斯坦1960年纽约爱乐版将作品当作炫技之作，终曲速度最快，呈现彻底的胜利感；普列文1965年伦敦交响乐团版则在精炼与驱动力之间取得平衡，慢乐章被延展至耳语般的低语。文章聚焦于指挥家对终曲速度及结尾性质（真诚凯旋还是被迫欢呼）的不同诠释，文本在第三个版本介绍处被截断。

山田和樹 ～N響やバーミンガム市響で矢代作品を指揮して 「交響曲」は自筆譜で演奏させていただいたのですが、その筆致をよく見てみると、一音一音にすごく確信がある。 最初に指揮した矢代作品である「ピアノ協奏曲」（演奏：NHK交響楽団／ピアノ：河村尚子）や、昨年バーミンガム市響と「交響曲」を演奏したときのエピソードを交えて、矢代作品のオリジナリティについて語っている。（取材・文＝西村祐） 河村尚子 ～「ピアノ協奏曲」を二度演奏して ご自身がピアノの名手であったこともあり、「ピアノ協奏曲」でもピアニストに要求されるものがとても大きいのです。（中略）たくさんの音色を描いていかなければならない。 「ピアノ協奏曲」を指揮者の下野竜也さん、山田和樹さんと共演して以来、「ピアノ・ソナタ」や小品にも取り組むようになった河村さん。「ピアノ協奏曲」においては、繊細さをきわめるような情景から、暴力的でアグレッシヴなシーンまで、常に音色を変化させていかなければならない。その多彩さこそが矢代作品の特徴のひとつだという。 上村文乃 ～2025年に初演者だった堤剛さんの代奏をして （チェロ協奏曲は）チェロのレチタティーヴォ（朗唱）と歌が非常に印象的です。（中略）オリエンタルな空気を感じつつ、西洋的な美や趣きがあるように感じられます。 日本に勢いのあった1960年に作曲された「チェロ協奏曲」。その時代性へ思いを寄せ、矢代と同級生である黛敏郎の無伴奏チェロ作品《BUNRAKU》を引き合いに出しながら、作品の魅力や音のつくりかたの細部などに言及している。   堤剛さんの弾く「チェロ協奏曲」が収録されたアルバム 矢代秋雄の関連本 「音楽の友」2026年10月号（9月18日発売）。特別企画として「没後50年記念 矢代秋雄の世界」を掲載 飾らず率直に綴られた、みずみずしい息吹を味わえる矢代秋雄の名エッセイ集 矢代秋雄 特設ページ 関連記事「ヨーロッパとのはてしない距離──矢代秋雄の孤独」
items._cn_summary: 本文为日本作曲家矢代秋雄没后五十周年纪念活动的新闻稿与音乐家访谈摘录。文章介绍了矢代在巴黎师从梅西安等大师的学习经历，以及其作品在钢琴协奏曲、交响曲、奏鸣曲等领域的特点。文中汇集了野平一郎、青柳いづみこ、山田和樹、河村尚子、上村文乃等音乐家对矢代作品的回忆与解读，涉及其作品中的法国学院派技法与日本元素的融合。作为二十世纪日本战后音乐的重要代表，矢代秋雄的作品在管弦乐法与和声语言上具有现代作曲的探索性。本文侧重纪念性回顾与演出信息推介，并非深度的乐评分析。

items._cn_summary: 这是一档名为Race The Sky的广播节目第026期，主持人Cliff Furnald。节目以杂烩形式呈现来自不同地区的音乐片段，涵盖90年间的各类曲目，包括David Bowie、Cream等主流摇滚艺人，以及来自非洲的Dawda Jobarteh、Alhaji Waziri Oshomah，葡萄牙的Eneida Marta，中东的Issa Murad等世界音乐艺人，还有Montparnasse Musique、Justin Adams & Mauro Duarte等融合项目。节目本身并非专辑乐评，而是电台播放列表式的曲目罗列，缺乏对音乐本身的深入分析与评论。世界音乐元素虽与用户口味部分契合，但整体编排偏向轻松杂烩风格，缺乏实验性与创新性，信息量极为有限。
